title: Ethosuximide in WWOX-related epilepsy
summary: In one mouse study, ethosuximide pretreatment lowered PTZ-provoked seizure scores. The result leaves WWOX specificity, spontaneous seizure control and benefit in children with WWOX-DEE unestablished.
evidence: Cheng et al. reported lower PTZ-provoked seizure scores in Wwox-null mice (Figure 7B). LEGEND’s re-reading of the group means found that most separation occurred late. Individual trajectories were unavailable.
Clinical evidence in childhood absence epilepsy concerns a different seizure syndrome.
limits: The mouse result leaves effects on spontaneous seizures, development and benefit in WWOX-DEE unresolved.

sources.label: Cheng et al. Wwox deficiency and seizure susceptibility in mice, Figure 7B. PMID 32000863.
Glauser et al. Randomised trial in childhood absence epilepsy. PMID 20164429.

graph.evidence: Lower PTZ seizure scores in Wwox-null mice.
graph.inference: Antiseizure signal in this PTZ assay.
graph.hypothesis: Wwox loss may modify the drug response.

inference: The result supports an effect on induced seizures in this mouse model. Baseline differences and low scores in comparator groups limit interpretation of the apparent genotype specificity.
hypothesis: Ethosuximide could have a different effect in Wwox-deficient animals. The data leave open both a general antiseizure effect and the identity of any channel mediating the response.
experiment: Compare treated and untreated groups across genotypes at the same age. Measure the treatment-by-genotype interaction and whether any effect extends to spontaneous seizures.
